title.narrative: Support for partners' and beneficiaries trips to the Pope's visit

description.narrative: The Democratic Republic of Congo has been experiencing armed conflicts for three decades of war. The nature of these armed conflicts has evolved according to different times and different actors. These various armed conflicts are among the bloodiest of the end of the 20th century and the beginning of the 21st century. They have led to heinous crimes: millions of deaths, large-scale rape and sexual violence, massive human rights violations, systematic looting of natural resources, widespread poverty, etc. Nowadays efforts are undertaken by the Congolese State to bring peace in the East of the DRC. State, organizational, private, and religious actors join forces with the Congolese State to provide multi-sectoral responses to the needs and challenges related to post-conflict pacification and socio-economic development. It is in this context that Pope Francis made a visit to the DRC from January 31 to February 3. Working for peace and socio-economic development requires active and dynamic people who know the needs of the population, and who can inspire confidence in them for participatory actions in individual and collective care. It is in this vision that fits the actions of CAFOD which lives daily alongside the Congolese population by providing support. Taking advantage of Pope Francis' visit to Kinshasa, CAFOD, in partnership with Caritas Goma, Caritas Bukavu, CDJP and Centre Olame, enabled certain victims of armed conflict and survivors of rape and sexual violence to travel to Kinshasa to meet the Pope, and thus bear witness to the face of the World on the atrocities of which they were victims during these armed conflicts.
